item.title: Otti approves 25% salary increase for Assembly workers
item.description: …FENRAD urges gov to extend salary review to other workers By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The Foundation for Environmental Rights Advocacy and Development (FENRAD) has urged Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, to extend the salary improvement approved for legislative workers to other categories of public servants, including teachers, healthcare professionals and local government employees. The call followed the governor’s approval of a 25 per cent implementation of the Consolidated Legislative Salary Structure (CONLESS) for eligible workers of the Abia State House of Assembly and the Assembly Service Commission. The new salary structure, which takes effect from January 2027, reportedly makes Abia the first state in the South-East to adopt CONLESS for parliamentary workers. The Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Njoku Ukoha, disclosed the approval in a statement on Wednesday, saying it followed recommendations by a committee set up to work out the implementation of the salary structure. CONLESS is the approved remuneration framework for legislative workers in the National Assembly, state Houses of Assembly and their respective service commissions. Its implementation has remained outstanding in several states despite demands by parliamentary workers. Reacting in a statement on Wednesday, FENRAD’s Executive Director, Comrade Nelson Nnanna Nwafor, commended Otti for the approval, describing it as a step towards improving workers’ welfare, addressing remuneration disparities and strengthening legislative administration. He, however, urged the state government to adopt an inclusive approach to workers’ welfare by extending comparable salary improvement measures to other Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs). According to him, teachers, healthcare workers, local government employees, administrative personnel and other public servants also deserve improved remuneration, decent working conditions and institutional support. While acknowledging the distinct remuneration framework for legislative workers, Nwafor said its implementation should not exclude other categories of public servants from government efforts to improve their welfare. FENRAD also called for transparent implementation of the approved 25 per cent adjustment from January 2027, adequate budgetary provisions, periodic salary reviews and regular engagement with organised labour and civil society groups. The organisation said good governance should be measured not only by infrastructure development and policy announcements but also by the extent to which government decisions improve workers’ living conditions, dignity and economic security. item.title: Kwankwaso and I have failed if anyone remains in IDP camps after 18 months — Obi
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has promised to tackle Nigeria’s displacement crisis, declaring that his administration would have failed if any Nigerian remained in an Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camp 18 months after assuming office. Obi gave the assurance while speaking in Jos, the Plateau State capital, on Wednesday, where he pledged to prioritise national unity and security if elected president in the 2027 general election. He lamented the divisions among Nigerians along ethnic and religious lines, insisting that national unity was essential to addressing the country’s challenges. According to him, his administration would focus on uniting the country and ensuring the safety of citizens, particularly in communities affected by persistent killings and displacement. “Our commitment is to unite Nigeria because today there is no unity, we are divided along tribal lines, religious lines, and that should not be, we are Nigerians. “Number two is to secure Nigeria. It’s our priority to ensure that Nigerians live in safety. In a place like Plateau and Benue where people are being killed daily, I assure you that no mother will cry again for her children. I assure you that no woman will feel the pain of losing a husband, neither will the father feel the pain of losing a wife,” he said. The former Anambra State governor stressed that his administration would not tolerate a situation in which Nigerians remained displaced long after he assumed office. “I have said it, and I will repeat it that after one year to 18 months in office, if any Nigerian remains in an IDP camp, we have failed,” he declared. Obi, who said he was familiar with the security challenges confronting communities in Plateau State, cited his visits to Bokkos, Mangu and Barkin Ladi as evidence of his understanding of the plight of affected residents. “No other presidential candidate has been to Bokkos, Mangu, and Barkin Ladi, so I know the pain that people are going through,” he said. He also expressed confidence that a joint administration with former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso as vice-president would tackle kidnapping and insecurity across the country. “Let me assure you that with Kwankwaso and I as the president and vice president of this country, nobody will kidnap school children and go into the bush,” Obi said. item.title: Brazil Electoral Court Fines Meta $1.3mn In Lula-Bolsonaro Spat
item.description: Brazil’s electoral court ruled Tuesday that Meta had to pay a fine of about $1.3 million for failing to comply with court orders after President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva alleged the tech giant tipped the scales toward his rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, during the latest presidential election. Leftist leader Lula had accused Meta of “algorithmic manipulation” favoring Bolsonaro in the run-up to the October 25 runoff vote, in which he surprisingly prevailed despite coming in second during the first-round ballot. Brazil’s President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva gestures during a meeting of the National Council for the Industrialisation of Critical and Strategic Minerals at the Planalto Palace in Brasília on November 5, 2026. (Photo by Evaristo Sa / AFP) | Evaristo Sa / AFP The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unanimously ruled to impose a fine of 7.5 million reais (around $1.3 million) on Meta, the parent company of Facebook, WhatsApp and Telegram, finding the company missed deadlines and lacked transparency in its investigation. However, the court’s reporting judge Marco Aurelio said the judicial body had not found evidence of any “deliberate action to skew the election.” This illustration photograph shows the Brazilian flag displayed on a smartphone screen in front of a screen displaying the logo of US technology company Meta in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on October 19, 2026. Photo by MAURO PIMENTEL / AFP Meta had denied the accusations but acknowledged that some of Lula’s campaign ads had been mistakenly deactivated due to technical errors. “We are going to have to regulate them,” Lula said of social media companies after his electoral victory. After refusing to acknowledge his loss in the runoff, Flavio Bolsonaro fled Brazil to the United States amid an ongoing investigation into him for alleged money laundering. item.title: Tinubu: Anambra RHA mobilises 143,000 vote canvassers
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Renewed Hope Ambassadors (RHA) in Anambra State have mobilised no fewer than 143,000 vote canvassers across the state’s 5,720 polling units to campaign for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general elections. The state coordinator of RHA, Chief Okey Ezenwa, disclosed this during a meeting of the organisation’s zonal and local government coordinators. Ezenwa said each polling unit had 25 canvassers prepared to drive grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election. “The Anambra State chapter of RHA is fully prepared for the 16 January 2027 presidential election. Our coordinators are fully on ground in the 21 Local Government Areas and the 326 wards,” he said. He disclosed that an 11-member local government committee and a 10-member ward steering committee had also been established to strengthen the organisation’s coordination and mobilisation efforts. According to him, the meeting resolved to convene a separate meeting with all APC National Assembly and State Assembly candidates in Anambra to agree on a clear strategic direction, particularly amid concerns over the perceived inactivity of the party’s state chapter. Ezenwa reaffirmed that the RHA would serve as a major political structure supporting APC candidates in the presidential, National Assembly and State Assembly elections. He also directed zonal, local government and ward coordinators to intensify grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election. The RHA coordinator expressed the organisation’s commitment to mobilising support for the successful conduct of the forthcoming presidential campaign rallies in the state. He commended the Director-General of RHA and Governor of Imo State, Hope Uzodimma, for his efforts in mobilising support for President Tinubu across the country. item.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak exceeds 11,000 cases
item.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo’s worst-ever outbreak of Ebola has now reached more than 11,000 confirmed cases, official Congolese figures showed on Wednesday, as armed conflict hampers the response. The 17th outbreak of the virus in the DRC’s history was officially declared in May but experts believe it emerged weeks or even months earlier. It has infected 11,042 people in the DRC and caused 5,387 deaths, according to the National Institute of Public Health. Around 2,990 people have recovered from Ebola, which is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids and causes severe hemorrhagic fever. Ebola has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the last 50 years. The worst outbreak previously recorded in the DRC killed nearly 2,300 people out of 3,500 cases between 2018 and 2020. The latest outbreak began in northeastern Ituri province and has since spread to seven other provinces, with most cases concentrated in Ituri and North Kivu. Cases have also been reported in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria. No approved vaccines or treatments exist currently for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the latest outbreak. Last month, the World Health Organization announced that Ervebo, a vaccine approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, would be put through a full human trial in the DRC to see if it offered any cross-protection against Bundibugyo. Security in eastern DRC is another challenge in fighting the health crisis. Ituri province is one of the most volatile and clashes between armed groups and violence against health workers regularly occur. A health centre treating Ebola patients was set on fire on Sunday by youths in Lolwa in Ituri province, health authorities said. Clashes between local militia on the same day temporarily suspended the health response in the area of Fataki, according to the UN. Islamic State-affiliated rebels from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) have carried out deadly attacks in several areas of Ituri, Haut-Uele and North Kivu in recent days, local and security sources said. item.title: ADC cannot stop Tinubu, APC will win all 36 states — Adeyeye
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — The Chairman of the Nigerian Ports Authority, Senator Dayo Adeyeye, has dismissed the African Democratic Congress (ADC) as a serious threat to President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, predicting that the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) will win all 36 states. Adeyeye, who is also the National Chairman of the South-West Agenda for Asiwaju (SWAGA), said the ADC lacked the political structure, grassroots influence and electoral strength to challenge the ruling party. He also questioned the political strength of the ADC’s presidential candidate, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, alleging that he lacked sufficient support even in his home state of Adamawa. Adeyeye spoke with journalists in Ado-Ekiti on Wednesday while assessing the political landscape ahead of the 2027 general election. He dismissed suggestions that the APC was apprehensive about the opposition, describing such claims as unfounded. According to him, the ADC has yet to demonstrate sufficient political strength at the state and National Assembly levels to pose a credible challenge to the ruling party. “How can the APC be afraid of anything with the political atmosphere we have now? I said over three months ago that President Tinubu was likely to win all the 36 states, and I am becoming increasingly convinced that it will happen. “ADC is a party without a governor in any of the 36 states. How many members does it have in the National Assembly? How many state assemblies does it control? You cannot compare a party without a demonstrable political structure with the APC,” he said. The former senator argued that Atiku’s presidential ambition was further weakened by what he described as inadequate political backing in Adamawa State. He alleged that neither the state governor nor prominent political figures in Adamawa had demonstrated substantial support for the former vice-president. “Atiku is from Adamawa, but the governor of his state is not supporting him. The legislature in the state has not witnessed any significant movement to the ADC. How do you intend to challenge and defeat an incumbent president when you cannot establish a formidable political base in your own state?” he asked. Adeyeye said SWAGA was established to consolidate Tinubu’s political base in the South-West, stressing that strong support at home was essential for any presidential candidate seeking national acceptance. He maintained that Tinubu had built a formidable political foundation across the South-West, adding that the president’s support base had continued to expand beyond the region. On the economy, Adeyeye acknowledged the hardship facing Nigerians but argued that the removal of fuel subsidy and the unification of the foreign exchange market had prevented the country from sliding into a deeper economic crisis. item.title: Customs intercepts six pangolins, two die in Oyo
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Federal Operations Unit (FOU), Zone ‘A’, of the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has intercepted six pangolins at Eruwa-Oni in Oyo State in a renewed crackdown on the illegal trafficking of endangered wildlife species. The interception, which took place at about 3 a.m. on Sunday, November 8, 2026, followed an intelligence-led patrol by Customs operatives. The suspected traffickers reportedly abandoned the animals and fled upon sighting the patrol team. The six pangolins were recovered alive and transported to the Unit’s headquarters in Ikeja, Lagos. However, two died shortly after arrival, leaving four surviving animals. The Customs Service subsequently handed over the four surviving pangolins and the carcasses of the two dead animals to relevant wildlife authorities for documentation and further necessary action. The handover was conducted by the Deputy Comptroller in charge of Enforcement, DC A.O. Oguntuase, on behalf of the Comptroller of FOU Zone ‘A’, Lagos. The Unit reiterated that protecting endangered species was a shared responsibility and urged members of the public to provide credible and timely information to assist law enforcement agencies in identifying and apprehending those involved in the illegal capture, possession, transportation and trafficking of protected wildlife. It also reaffirmed its commitment to suppressing smuggling and other forms of illicit trade, while strengthening collaboration with relevant agencies to protect Nigeria’s natural heritage. item.title: Awujale palace not under siege – Ogun police
item.description: The Police Command in Ogun has dismissed reports alleging that the Awujale Palace in Ijebu-Ode was under siege by thugs and miscreants. This is contained in a statement issued by DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, the command’s spokesperson in Abeokuta on Wednesday. According to Babaseyi, the deployment is a preventive security measure aimed at safeguarding lives and property and preventing any breakdown of public peace. He added that an Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) was deployed to supervise and coordinate the security arrangement at the palace. The police spokesperson also clarified that one person had been invited following a written petition containing allegations against him. According to him, the person honoured the invitation, was questioned over the allegations and subsequently released on self-recognisance, while investigations continued. Babaseyi stressed that the invitation was part of a legitimate investigative process and should not be interpreted as an indication of guilt. He reiterated the command’s commitment to professionalism, impartiality, the rule of law and respect for the rights of all individuals. “Members of the public should remain calm, disregard misleading reports and avoid circulating unverified information capable of creating tension or disturbing public peace. “The command is committed to protecting lives and property, maintaining public order and enforcing the law impartially across the state,” he said. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the Awujale stool became vacant in July 2025, following the death of Oba Sikiru Adetona at 91, after 65 years reign. item.title: Fossil Fuels ‘Must Go The Way Of The Dinosaurs’, UN Chief Tells World Leaders At COP31
item.description: UN chief Antonio Guterres on Wednesday accused oil and gas interests of blocking action on climate change and urged world leaders at COP31 to “end the fossil fuel addiction”. “Fossil fuels must go the way of the dinosaurs, but that won’t happen on its own. The dinosaurs did not have a lobby, but fossil fuels do,” Guterres said in Turkey at his final UN climate summit as secretary-general. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres railed against the oil and gas lobby on Wednesday, urging world leaders to “end the fossil fuel addiction” at a climate summit missing several prominent figures. The two-week COP31 talks kicked off in Turkey earlier this week with governments under pressure to tackle climate change after a year of searing heatwaves and wildfires in Europe, and deadly floods in Nepal. “The brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us,” Guterres told dozens of world leaders assembled at a sprawling expo centre in the Mediterranean city of Antalya. This handout photograph taken and released by Turkish Presidency Press Office on November 10, 2026, shows Turkey’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan (C,R) meeting with UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres (C,L) during the COP31 UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya. But few major breakthroughs are anticipated at the COP31 negotiations, which run until November 20, as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the US war with Iran and Russia’s conflict in Ukraine. Since agreeing in 2023 for the first time to transition away from fossil fuels — the main driver of climate change — nations have struggled to advance that goal at the annual COP conferences. “Fossil fuel interests keep making a killing, while killing our planet,” Guterres said, urging governments to tax the windfall profits of oil companies. “Fossil fuels must go the way of the dinosaurs, but that won’t happen on its own. The dinosaurs did not have a lobby, but fossil fuels do,” he said. “Their strategy is simple: Distort the science. Delay the policy. Delay the action. Delay the accountability. It’s time to kick the habit –- and end the fossil fuel addiction,” he said to applause. Swedish activist Greta Thunberg arrives at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, on November 10, 2026. Global fossil fuel emissions are projected to fall slightly in 2026 due to the expansion of renewable energy and the oil price shock sparked by the Iran war, researchers said Tuesday. Guterres, who has made the fight against climate change a central issue since taking office in 2017, is attending his last COP before his term ends in December. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Iran’s Masoud Pezeshkian are among the leaders due to speak during the “high-level segment” taking place on Wednesday and Thursday. item.title: El Nino Fuels Indonesia Fire Outbreak, Destroys 2.88 Million Hectares – Report
item.description: Fires in Indonesia driven partly by a strong El Nino have burned through 2.88 million hectares (7.1 million acres) so far in 2026, a monitor analysing satellite imagery told AFP on Wednesday. The burned area figure — 18 times the size of London — has increased nearly a million hectares since deforestation monitoring site Nusantara Atlas’s last update in September. Indonesia’s government has not provided official figures for areas burned since announcing 202,000 hectares had been razed by the end of July. The burning detected in analysis through the end of October is a conservative estimate, warned Nusantara Atlas founder David Gaveau, in part because smoke has obscured satellite images. But it already exceeds the full-year figure for 2019, previously the worst year on record in Nusantara Atlas data. Indonesia also experienced devastating fires in 2015, but the satellite imagery used then was different, making a direct comparison difficult. Volunteers spray water to extinguish a land fire at Terantang in Barito Kuala regency, South Kalimantan province, on November 7, 2026, following months of forest and land fires. (Photo by MUDA SAGALA / AFP) Still, the scale of destruction is clear, said Gaveau. “Basically, it’s a really bad year,” he said. The arrival of rain has brought some of the worst blazes under control, and monitoring shows the number of so-called hotspots starting to flatten or decline. But the figure for total burned area is likely to rise further given some fires are still burning, and as burn scars previously hidden by smoke become visible to satellites in coming months. Indonesia’s government previously said it needed more time to analyse data before issuing updated figures. AFP has asked for comment on the monitor’s latest data. Indonesia experiences fires every dry season, but this year’s blazes have been particularly severe in part due to an intense drought caused by the El Nino weather pattern. A firefighter sprays water to extinguish a wildfire burning organic-rich peatland, which smolders underground and releases dense smoke in Pulang Pisau Regency, in Central Kalimantan province on November 4, 2026. (Photo by REINA / AFP) Experts say the fires are also the result of decades of deforestation and the drying out of peatlands for plantations, making large swathes of land more vulnerable to flames. The fires have caused devastating local pollution that has sickened hundreds of thousands of people and sent haze into neighbouring countries, including Malaysia and Singapore. item.title: Man United close to deal with Pochettino to become next coach
item.description: Manchester United are reportedly closing in on an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick as head coach if the club decides to end his tenure. According to Sky Sports, the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager, who currently coaches the United States national team, is being lined up as Carrick’s potential successor, with discussions between the parties said to be at an advanced stage. Carrick reported to United’s Carrington training ground at around 7:45 am on Wednesday, with uncertainty continuing over his future at Old Trafford. The club’s hierarchy is expected to discuss his position at a meeting in Monaco on Wednesday, where chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are scheduled to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe. The meeting was initially arranged to review United’s performances this season, but Carrick’s position is now expected to feature prominently following the club’s disappointing start to the campaign. Berrada and Wilcox are expected to present their recommendations to Ratcliffe, who oversees football operations at the club, before a final decision is reached on the head coach’s future. Sky Sports News understands that United would have to pay approximately £7m to release Pochettino from his recently signed contract with the United States national team, although the financial requirement is not considered an obstacle to the proposed appointment. Pochettino is reportedly prepared to take over if United decide to make a change, although he is currently scheduled to lead the United States against Haiti on Saturday. Meanwhile, former United captain Roy Keane has criticised Carrick’s leadership following the club’s recent performances. Keane said the under-pressure manager “talks a lot but doesn’t say much” and needs to “get moving” on improving the team after United’s late 4-4 draw against Aston Villa. United’s struggles have increased scrutiny on Carrick, with the club’s management now considering a potential change in the dugout. item.title: The Future of Business Payments in Africa: What Will Change by 2027?
item.description: In January 2026, one of the world’s biggest streamers walked up to a jewellery seller in Lagos Nigeria and tried to pay. IShowSpeed was in the middle of his Africa tour and had just passed 50 million YouTube subscribers while in Lagos. He picked out about $1,500 worth of jewellery and offered to pay with Apple Pay. The merchant said no. So he paid in USDT instead, a stablecoin, which is a digital token built to hold the value of the US dollar. A few days later, Tether’s Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Paolo Ardoino, shared the clip on X: “iShowspeed shopping with USDT in Nigeria.” Technically this was done via usdt to ngn swap. It was a fun moment. But look past the cameras and that one sale holds four big shifts in African business payments: Faster settlement: The seller was paid on the spot, not days later. Multi-currency business: A Nigerian merchant accepted dollar value from a foreign customer. Digital payments: No cash and no card machine, just a phone. New payment rails: A well-known global payment method did not fit. A newer one did. Now ask a harder question. If a jewellery seller can do all that in one sale, why does your business still wait days to pay a supplier or get paid by one? Here is how each of those four shifts will change African business payments by 2027. 1. Faster settlement becomes the baseline Within many African countries, money already moves in seconds. Africa’s instant payment systems reportedly processed transactions worth $1.98 trillion in 2025, according to data from a GSMA mobile money report. Despite this huge demand, cross-border payments are where businesses still feel the wait. An international wire transfer typically takes 3–5 business days to arrive and costs about 8% of the entire transaction value on average, according to the world bank. A stablecoin payment typically settles in under a day and costs about 3%. “Speed is easy to promise. What businesses really need is speed they can trust, with licensing, compliance and clean records built in from day one.” Ebieroma Morris, Co-founder and CIO, Quidax 2. More businesses run in many currencies Africa has about 42 currencies. A business that sells into three countries and buys from a fourth may deal with five currencies before lunch. That used to be a headache for large companies only. By 2027, it will be normal for mid-sized businesses too. A fashion brand in Lagos selling to buyers in Accra and London, or a manufacturer in Nairobi paying suppliers in Shenzhen, will receive, hold and pay out in several currencies. Three things will change for finance teams: Holding balances in more than one currency, and deciding each day what to keep and what to convert. Using dollar-linked stablecoins as a shared balance for paying and receiving abroad, then converting to local currency when needed. Checking the books daily, or in real time : When money moves in minutes, month-end reconciliation, meaning matching your records against the bank and the blockchain, is too slow.

item.title: FG Commissions Three CNG Facilities In Kano
item.description: The Federal Government has commissioned three Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) infrastructure facilities in Kano State, as part of efforts to expand access to cleaner and cheaper energy and reduce transportation costs. The facilities, developed by Rolling Energy Limited with support from the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF), comprise a 300,000-standard cubic metres per day Liquefied Compressed Natural Gas (LCNG) distribution hub and a retail station at Tamburawa, Dawakin Kudu Local Government Area, as well as a 21,000-standard cubic metres per day LCNG daughter and retail station at Hotoro, Tarauni LGA. Speaking at the commissioning ceremony, the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo, said the projects represented the Federal Government’s commitment to translating Nigeria’s abundant gas resources into tangible economic benefits for citizens. Ekpo, who was represented by a senior government official, said the facilities would strengthen gas distribution, deepen penetration in Kano and neighbouring communities, support businesses and transportation, and create new economic opportunities. He said the Tamburawa hub would provide integrated LNG storage, regasification and CNG distribution services, including the capacity to supply daughter stations, while the retail outlets would ensure that the product reached consumers directly. “Together, these three facilities demonstrate the complete philosophy of our domestic gas agenda: building the infrastructure to receive and distribute gas, while simultaneously creating the last-mile outlets that make the product accessible to Nigerians,” he said. Ekpo during the opening of two CNG daughter stations capable of dispensing CNG to more than 2,500 vehicles and 50 trucks daily in Kano, on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. The minister said the projects aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, which, according to him, seeks to move the country from policy formulation to the delivery of critical infrastructure. “His charge to us is clear: we must move from policies to projects, from plans to infrastructure, and from gas reserves beneath our soil to affordable energy that actually reaches our homes, businesses, industries and transportation systems,” he said. Ekpo added that government was determined to mobilise private sector investment to accelerate the development of the country’s gas infrastructure. He commended Rolling Energy, MDGIF, regulators, investors and other technical partners for their contributions to the projects. Also speaking, the Executive Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, Barr. Ismaeel Ahmed, said the expansion of CNG infrastructure across the country showed that investments in the sector were yielding results. item.title: Iran lists Argentina navy, air force as terrorist organisations
item.description: Iran’s foreign ministry on Wednesday designated Argentina’s navy and air force as terrorist organisations, following a similar move by Buenos Aires months earlier. In late March, Argentina designated Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of the military, as a terror organisation, citing the IRGC’s support for Lebanese militant group Hezbollah. Buenos Aires says the group was involved in a 1994 attack on the AMIA Jewish community centre in Buenos Aires that killed 85 people and injured hundreds more. In 2019, Iran passed a law that could see the country retaliate against any state that designates its military forces as terrorist organisations. Tehran “deems the Argentine Navy and the Argentine Air Force subject to the aforementioned law and its provisions, and designates them as terrorist organisations,” the ministry said in a statement. It was not immediately clear what practical effect the designation would have. Earlier this month, Iran made a similar move designating UK’s MI6 as a hostile group and the country’s Royal Navy and Royal Air Force as terrorist organisations. It came after the UK designated the IRGC as a terror organisation in July. The post Iran lists Argentina navy, air force as terrorist organisations appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Peace Accord under threat as 26 states, FCT record 109 violations – NPC
item.description: …political violence, fake news dominate breaches as Kaduna, Edo, Enugu emerge flashpoints …gunmen disrupt opposition gatherings, threats of AK-47 attacks, religious intolerance raise fears By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The National Peace Accord signed by political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections is facing an early test, with 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory recording 109 violations in just 10 weeks, raising fears of escalating political violence, intimidation and misinformation as campaigns gather momentum. The National Peace Committee (NPC), in its latest monitoring report covering August 19 to October 27, warned that recurring armed disruptions of political activities, threats by political officeholders and the growing spread of fake political information could undermine peaceful campaigns and threaten the credibility of the 2027 elections. The report identified political violence and thuggery as the leading violations, accounting for 33 incidents, while misinformation and disinformation followed closely with 29 cases. Attacks on political activities and campaign materials accounted for another 19 incidents, while intimidation and threats recorded 15 cases. Kaduna emerged as the state with the highest number of reported violations, recording nine incidents, while Edo, Enugu and the FCT recorded seven each. The committee specifically identified Enugu, Oyo, Edo and Cross River as areas requiring urgent attention over recurring armed disruptions, while Benue and Kogi were flagged over security risks surrounding political convoys and movements. The development comes barely three months after 19 political parties signed the National Peace Accord in Abuja on August 18, committing themselves to peaceful, issue-based campaigns and rejecting violence, threats and intimidation ahead of the elections. Under the electoral timetable released by the Independent National Electoral Commission, presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027, while governorship and state House of Assembly elections will be held on February 6, 2027. Campaigns for the presidential and National Assembly elections commenced on August 19, while those for governorship and State Assembly polls began on September 9. item.title: Meghan Keeps Low Profile On First Trip After Father’s Arrest
item.description: Meghan Markle appeared in public for the first time Tuesday since her estranged father was charged for alleged possession of child sexual abuse images — keeping a low profile as she visited Brussels with her husband Prince Harry. The Duke and Duchess of Sussex were greeted by a cluster of photographers on arrival at the EU parliament for an event about the dangers children face online. Meghan’s father Thomas Markle was arrested in Florida on Friday and charged with one count of possession of child sexual abuse material — and she did not reply to a shouted question seeking a comment. The couple had been due to give a joint speech, but only Harry spoke at the opening of an installation honouring 50 children who died because of online abuse and exploitation, dubbed the “Lost Screen Memorial”. Britain’s Prince Harry (L), Duke of Sussex and his wife Meghan (R), Duchess of Sussex, arrive at the European Parliament in Brussels on November 10, 2026, to attend the opening of “Lost Screen Memorial”. Photo by JOHN THYS / AFP An unnamed source told the UK’s Daily Telegraph newspaper that Meghan is “just not strong enough emotionally to be doing any public speaking” following her father’s arrest. The couple projected calm when they arrived on Tuesday morning. Dressed in all black with a small poppy pin — the symbol of remembrance for soldiers who died in battle — Meghan held tightly on to Harry’s hand. The duke was dressed in a sombre dark blue suit, also with a poppy and dark-coloured tie. Meghan appeared smiling next to Harry as she met European Parliament President Roberta Metsola and Spanish EU lawmaker Antonio Lopez-Isturiz. The visit also marked the couple’s first appearance together at a public event abroad, since returning to live in Britain following six years in the United States. ‘Disturbing’ allegations Meghan’s 82-year-old father was taken into custody by FBI agents Friday at the retirement home where he lives in Lakeland, Florida and has been ordered to undergo a psychiatric examination. On Tuesday, US Attorney Bill Essayli posted to X that he had requested Thomas Markle be detained because the court ordered him to wear a monitoring device but “he allegedly cut the bracelet off”. US Magistrate Judge Lindsay Griffin ordered Thomas Markle “detained pending the resolution of this case” on Tuesday, writing “the defendant violated the conditions of his pretrial release”. The US Justice Department said Markle allegedly “kept child sexual abuse material (CSAM), including sexually explicit photographs of himself with prepubescent girls, in two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented for nearly two decades”. Markle could face up to 20 years in prison if convicted. British tabloids reported last month that pictures of child sex abuse had been found at Thomas Markle’s former home in the Philippines, allegations later confirmed by police but denied by the duchess’s father. item.title: Kudus boost as desperate Ghana seek AFCON redemption
item.description: Troubled Ghana have received a boost with Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Mohammed Kudus available for a must-win Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Somalia on Thursday. Injuries ruled the 26-year-old out of the 2026 World Cup, and he also missed AFCON losses to the Ivory Coast and the Gambia two months ago. Veteran captain and striker Jordan Ayew, who plays for English second-tier club Sheffield United, is another returnee as Ghana seek redemption after a dismal start in Group C. However, the four-time African champions must do without injured Manchester City winger Antoine Semenyo when they face opponents 130 places lower in the world rankings. The loss to the Ivorians in Abidjan was not unexpected, but the 4-2 defeat at home to the Gambians after building a two-goal lead led to Portuguese coach Carlos Queiroz resigning. Matchdays three and four begin on Thursday and conclude on Tuesday. Countries meet each other at home and away, but Ghana will be at ‘home’ twice due to the security situation in Somalia. Somali preparations at a university stadium in Accra were disrupted when security personnel ordered the squad to move to another location. While Ghana seek six points in Essipong to get back into contention ahead of the final two matchdays next March, co-leaders Ivory Coast and Gambia also meet twice, in Abidjan and Bakau. AFP Sport highlights Ghana, Nigeria, Cape Verde and Tunisia — four teams in trouble after poor starts to qualifying. GHANA Swede Kim Lars Bjorkegren, the coach of the Ghana women’s national team, has been put in temporary charge of the men’s team while the search for a permanent replacement continues. He had mixed results at the recent women’s AFCON in Morocco. They lost to eventual champions Cameroon in the quarter-finals, but are still contenders for the 2027 World Cup in Brazil. After losing narrowly in the Gambia, the Ocean Stars of Somalia held three-time African champions Ivory Coast goalless for 88 minutes before conceding twice. NIGERIA Having struggled to overcome modest Madagascar at home on matchday one in Group L, lacklustre Nigeria crashed to a 3-0 away loss against Guinea-Bissau, a country ranked 124th in the world. On top of failing to qualify for the last two World Cup tournaments, the humiliating AFCON defeat led to an outcry with former star Segun Odegbami lamenting “a dive to new depths”. Nigeria must face Tanzania — auotmatic qualifiers as co-hosts with Kenya and Uganda — without injured star striker Victor Osimhen, the 2023 African Footballer of the Year. CAPE VERDE Football fans at the 2026 World Cup fell in love with the tiny island nation off the west coast of Africa after they held Spain, then took Argentina to extra time in a last-32 tie. But the Blue Sharks could miss a second successive AFCON after losing away to Mali and at home to Rwanda. They now face fellow Group K strugglers Liberia twice. item.title: AFCONQ: Nigeria vs Tanzania – date, time and where to watch
item.description: The Super Eagles of Nigeria will return to action on Friday, November 13, when they host Tanzania in a crucial 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying encounter. The Group L matchday-three fixture will take place at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, as Nigeria seek to strengthen their chances of qualifying for the continental tournament. The encounter is scheduled to kick off at 5:00 pm Nigerian time (WAT). Nigeria head into the fixture needing a victory after a mixed start to their qualifying campaign, having recorded one win and one defeat in their opening two matches. Where Nigeria stand in Group L The Super Eagles currently occupy second position in Group L with three points from two matches, three points behind leaders Guinea-Bissau, who have won both their opening fixtures. Nigeria opened their campaign with a 2-1 victory over Madagascar in Uyo before suffering a 3-0 defeat to Guinea-Bissau away from home. Tanzania sit third with one point, level with bottom-placed Madagascar, but ahead on goal difference. The stakes are particularly high for Nigeria because Tanzania have already secured automatic qualification for the 2027 tournament as one of the co-hosts alongside Kenya and Uganda. Consequently, Nigeria, Guinea-Bissau and Madagascar are competing for the remaining qualification spot available in the group. A victory over Tanzania would take Nigeria to six points and strengthen their position in the race for qualification. Where to watch Nigeria vs Tanzania Football fans in Nigeria can follow the encounter live on SuperSport. When is the return fixture? Nigeria will travel to Tanzania for the return fixture on Tuesday, November 17, as both countries meet again in quick succession. The two encounters could prove important for Nigeria’s qualification ambitions, with the Super Eagles needing to collect maximum points to avoid falling further behind Guinea-Bissau. The 2027 Africa Cup of Nations will be staged across Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from June 19 to July 17, 2027. item.title: Nigerian newspapers review: [APC] Security of lives, property to top Tinubu’s 2nd term agenda

item.title: Fight or flight? Trump mixes signals after midterms
item.description: President Donald Trump’s political mantra is “fight, fight, fight.” But he has given decidedly mixed messages about whether he will do so after Republicans were hammered in the midterms. In the week since becoming a lame duck, Trump named the hardline architect of his migration crackdown as his chief of staff, while admitting his deportation policy was too tough. The 80-year-old raised eyebrows when he publicly asked Ultimate Fighting Championship boss Dana White to be his new press secretary — then claimed he was just joking. He has admitted that the Iran war was largely to blame for the midterms rout. But he has strongly backed Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth’s battle against impeachment. And despite saying on election night that he’d accept the results of the Democratic sweep, he has reverted to type and revived baseless claims of election fraud. “One of the characteristics of Donald Trump is that he changes his mind on a dime,” Democratic Senator Chris Coons told CNN. “He’ll be praising someone on Monday, firing them on Tuesday, and pretending he never knew them on Wednesday. So it’s hard to predict exactly what Donald Trump is going to do.” – ‘Too tough’ – Democrats have promised to rein in Trump and launch a series of investigations into corruption and abuse of power. He could face a third impeachment. But for a president supposedly facing his last stand, he has at times struck a surprisingly conciliatory tone. As results came in, he congratulated Democrats on seizing Congress and said he could work with them. Instead of a press conference the next day, he gave reporters a tour of his new White House ballroom — sparking speculation he might spend the rest of his term on his building projects. But the signs of volatility were still there. In the Oval Office, Trump placed a red baseball cap saying “veto” on his desk. And when Trump announced on Friday that ultraloyalist Stephen Miller would replace Susie Wiles as his chief of staff, it seemed that the gloves were finally off. The brains behind the masked immigration raids that left two Americans dead, Miller has also been instrumental in using executive orders to help Trump bypass Congress. Yet in an interview the same day — though broadcast on Sunday — Trump conceded voters had been turned off by the aggressive deportation push. “I think it was too tough,” Trump told the CBS News “60 Minutes” program. Still, the chances of Trump doing a deal with Democrats — possibly even for an amnesty for undocumented migrants — remain low. “It doesn’t seem likely. Not with this decision to have Stephen Miller running the show,” Sarah Binder, a senior fellow in governance studies at the Brookings Institution, said in a panel discussion this week. – ‘Violent fighter’ – Trump’s astonishing announcement on Saturday that he wanted “violent fighter and warrior” Dana White to be his new spokesman also seemed to signal a war footing. If it seemed too ironic to be true, it was. A day later Trump said he was “kidding.”
